text.p: Following are the main stories in the Croatian newspapers on Thursday:
- The Croatian government issued 348,000 documents to Serb residents of the Danube region to enable them to vote in the April 13 elections.
- The leader of the ruling HDZ party Ivic Pasalic says results of the fight against economic crime and corruption will be revealed soon.
- Croatia ratifies a ship-building contract with Iran worth 109 million kuna.
- Croatia expects 25,000 Russian tourists in its Adriatic summer resorts, a 100 percent increase compared to last year. Tourist giants want to attract Russians as they spend on average $150 daily.

- President Franjo Tudjman and Foreign Minister Mate Granic met for talks with Czech deputy prime minister Josef Zieleniec. The Croatian side emphasised the priority of completing the peaceful reintegration of Eastern Slavonia successfully, while Zieleniec expressed his support for Croatia to enter European integration processes as soon as posible, notably to join CEFTA (Central European Free Trade Agreement).

- Bread is still too expensive, but conditions to bring the price down have not been met, for example higher supply than demand of wheat, price of wheat per kilogram should not exceed 1.10 kuna and loans for the purchase of wheat at a nine per cent interest rate.
- Some 7,400 polling stations throughout the country await voters in the forthcoming elections on Sunday. Preliminary results are expected on Monday, April 14, at 1 a.m.
- Tourism Minister Niko Bulic predicts 26.5 million overnights this summer. "Tourism will give Croatia an extra leverage this year," Bulic said.

- The leader of the Social Democratic Party (former communists) Ivica Racan on accusations that Croatia is in jeopardy of a 'red danger' replies that the danger lies in discontent, warning that "poverty should not be the destiny of the majority of the citizens, and a comfortable life and arrogant behaviour a privilege of a minority".

- A group of 180 foreign journalists from 15 countries, accompanied with 10 TV crews, is touring Croatia at an invitation of The Croatia Tourist Association, to gain a better look at the country's tourism potential. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
